# ggPSE

**ggPSE** is a [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/)-based toolkit
for visualizing element-, group- or period-resolved data on the periodic
table of elements. Every function returns a standard `ggplot2` object -
so plots can be extended with themes, annotations, faceting, and
`patchwork`.

## Installation

``` r

# Install from GitHub (requires remotes)
remotes::install_github("VJGeiger/ggPSE")
```

If you want to plot with country flag badges 🇺🇸 🇮🇹 🇬🇧, also install
ggflags (not on CRAN, but GitHub):

``` r

remotes::install_github("rensa/ggflags")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Quick start

``` r

library(ggPSE)

# Blank periodic table
ggPSE()
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Visualization modes

### Numerated Tiles

The numeration can be switched on with `show_atomic_number = TRUE`,
default is `FALSE`to avoid crowded tiles.

``` r

ggPSE(show_atomic_number = TRUE)
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_numbering.png) \### Tile borders

Adapt the tile coloring as well as its borders for the whole PSE.

``` r

ggPSE(color_na = "white", tile_border = "gray40")
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_tiles.png)

### Show Selection

If you are interested ind displaying only a part of the PSE you can
specify this via the `periods` and `groups` as a default lanthanides and
actinides are always set to be displayed and have to be actively omitted
by using `lanthanides = FALSE`.

``` r

# Periods 4-6 with lanthanides
ggPSE(periods = c(4, 6), groups = c(3,4), lanthanides= FALSE, actinides = FALSE)
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_selection.png)

### Highlight elements

Color named subsets of elements with a legend entry per group.

``` r

ggPSE(highlight = list(
  list(symbols = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P"),
       color   = "#2166ac",
       label   = "Battery metals"),
  list(symbols = c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb", "Pr", "La", "Ce"),
       color   = "#e63946",
       label   = "Rare earth magnets")
))
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_custom_tiles.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Built-in element data

ggPSE ships with `ggpse_elements`, a data frame of 17 physical and
chemical properties for all 118 elements (IUPAC 2021, NIST WebBook,
Pauling 1960):

``` r

data(ggpse_elements)
ggPSE(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity",
      legend_title = "Electronegativity (Pauling)")
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_EN.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Data visualization

### Color Gradient

Map any numeric variable to a fill color gradient across all elements.

``` r

battery <- data.frame(
  symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P", "C"),
  importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.40, 0.35)
)

ggPSE(battery,
      value_col    = "importance",
      color_low    = "#f7fbff",
      color_high   = "#08306b",
      legend_title = "Battery relevance")
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_custom_col_grad.png)

The mapping can also be applied to a selection of the PSE.

``` r

data(ggpse_elements)
ggPSE(ggpse_elements[ggpse_elements$block == "d", ],
      value_col = "density_g_cm3", legend_title = "Density (g/cm3)")
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_TM_density.png)

It is also possible to customize the ggplots to multigradient scales for
better visualization.

``` r

data(ggpse_elements)

ggPSE(ggpse_elements,
      value_col    = "density_g_cm3",
      color_low    = "#2166ac",   
      color_high   = "#a50026",   
      legend_title = "Density (g/cm³)") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours  = c("#2166ac", "#1a9850", "#a50026"),
    na.value = "#f0f0f0",
    name     = "Density (g/cm³)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Elemental density across the periodic table") +
  ggplot2::theme(plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_density_multigrad.png)

### Bubble plot

Map a numeric variable to bubble size.

``` r

supply_risk <- data.frame(
  symbol = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Dy", "Pt", "Rh", "In", "Ga"),
  risk   = c(0.62, 0.91, 0.84, 0.88, 0.52, 0.70, 0.78, 0.65)
)
ggPSE_bubble(supply_risk, size_col = "risk", legend_title = "Supply risk")
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_bubbles.png)

### In-tile bar encoding

Draw a proportional bar inside each tile growing from a chosen edge
(`"bottom"`, `"top"`, `"left"`, or `"right"`).

``` r

ggPSE_bar(supply_risk, value_col = "risk",
          bar_side  = "bottom",
          bar_color = "#2166ac",
          legend_title = "Supply risk")
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_bars_bottom.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Donut Charts

One can add donuts per field to display distributions with element
resolution. With the `plot_all =TRUE` it is optional to display all
elements even those without data.

``` r

supply <- data.frame(
   symbol   = c("Li","Li","Li", "Co","Co", "Nd","Nd", "Pt"),
   category = c("CL","AU","AR", "CD","AU", "CN","RU", "ZA"),
   share    = c(0.60, 0.30, 0.10, 0.70, 0.30, 0.80, 0.20, 1.00)
 )

ggPSE(groups = c(3,12)) |>
gPSE_donut(supply, category_col = "category", share_col = "share", plot_all = FALSE)
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_donut.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Period and group profiles

The display of selected periods and rows with corresponding data can be
achieved via the
[`ggPSE_profile()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_profile.md)
function. Elements with no values are omitted.

``` r

ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity", period = 6)

# or

ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity", group = 12)

# or

ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity", lanthanides = TRUE)
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_profile_period_6.png)

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_profile_group_2.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Country-of-origin badges

Overlay country flags (via ggflags) or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 text codes. Up
to three flags per tile are supported. These tiles can be displayed with
a hierarchy (1st-2nd-3rd “place”). A legend is optional and can be
positioned around the plot.

``` r

supply <- data.frame(
  symbol  = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Pt"),
  country = c("CL", "CD", "CN", "ZA"),
  value   = c(0.70, 0.91, 0.85, 0.60)
)
ggPSE(supply, value_col = "value", legend_title = "Criticality") |>
  ggPSE_badge(supply, country_col = "country")
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_flags.png)

``` r

supply_multi <- data.frame(
  symbol  = c("Li", "Li", "Co", "Co", "Co", "Nd", "Pt"),
  country = c("CL", "AU", "CD", "AU", "ZM", "CN", "ZA"),
  value   = c(0.70, 0.70, 0.91, 0.91, 0.91, 0.85, 0.60)
)

ggPSE(supply_multi, value_col = "value",
      color_high = "#b2182b", legend_title = "Criticality") |>
  ggPSE_badge(supply_multi, country_col = "country")
  
 ggPSE(supply_multi, value_col = "value") |>
     ggPSE_badge(supply_multi, country_col = "country",
                 hierarchy = TRUE, hierarchy_scale = c(1.0, 0.6, 0.5), show_legend = TRUE, legend_position = "bottom")
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_flags_multi.png)![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_flags_multi_ranked.png)
—

## Interactive plots

The displayed values can be made into interactive plots with
[`ggPSE_interactive()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_interactive.md)
👉 [Interactive periodic table
example](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/interactive.html)

``` r

ggPSE_interactive(battery, value_col = "importance")

# or 

ggPSE_interactive(
  ggpse_elements,
  value_col    = "electronegativity",
  tooltip_cols = c("name", "atomic_weight", "block", "electronegativity"),
  legend_title = "Electronegativity (Pauling)"
)
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_interactive.gif)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Themes

There are four prebuilt themes available via
[`ggPSE_theme()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_theme.md).
\| Theme \| Description \| \|—\|—\| \| `"minimal"` \| White background,
simple\| \| `"dark"` \| Dark plot background \| \| `"publication"` \|
Minimal ink, transparent background, journal-ready \| \| `"crazy"` \|
Random color per tile, reproducible with `seed` \|

``` r

# Minimal
ggPSE() |> ggPSE_theme("minimal")

# Publication
ggPSE(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity") |>
  ggPSE_theme("publication")

# Crazy — reproducible
ggPSE() |> ggPSE_theme("crazy", seed = 42)
```

![](reference/figures/ggPSE_plot_theme_crazy.png)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Saving figures

Figures can be saved via the wrapper
[`ggPSE_save()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_save.md)
for ease. For more custom plots, `ggsave()` can be used as well.

``` r

data(ggpse_elemts)
p <- ggPSE(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity")

ggPSE_save(p, "electronegativity.png")   # PNG 18x14cm at 400dpi
ggPSE_save(p, "electronegativity.pdf")   # vector PDF
ggPSE_save(p, "electronegativity.svg")   # web SVG
ggPSE_save(p, "electronegativity.png", width = 24, height = 9, dpi = 600)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Experimental features

`ggPSE_sparkline()` and `ggPSE_spark_bar()` per-tile time series
sparklines was deemed too unstable and in need of further development.

Available on the `feature/sparkline` branch:

``` r

remotes::install_github("VJGeiger/ggPSE@feature/sparkline")
```

## Alternatives

### R alternatives

- [periodicdata](https://github.com/solarchemist/periodicdata): Rich on
  dataset for the periodic system in R.
- [PeriodicTable](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/PeriodicTable/index.html):
  Simplest alternative for a PSE.

### python alternatives

- [mendeelv](https://pypi.org/project/mendeleev/): Rich-dataset,
  feature-rich and optional interactive visualization.

# Package index

## Core plotting

Main periodic table functions

- [`ggPSE()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE.md) :
  Plot a periodic table with a continuous value overlay
- [`ggPSE_theme()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_theme.md)
  : Apply a pre-built theme to a periodic table plot
- [`ggPSE_save()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_save.md)
  : Save a periodic table plot with sensible defaults

## Encodings

Additional visual encoding layers

- [`ggPSE_bubble()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_bubble.md)
  : Plot a periodic table with bubble size encoding
- [`ggPSE_bar()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_bar.md)
  : Plot a periodic table with in-tile bar encoding
- [`ggPSE_donut()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_donut.md)
  : Overlay donut or pie charts on a periodic table

## Annotations

Overlay annotations on tiles

- [`ggPSE_badge()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_badge.md)
  : Overlay country-of-origin badges on a periodic table

## Analytical views

Period, group and trend profiles

- [`ggPSE_profile()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_profile.md)
  : Plot a single period, group, or f-block row with a trend line

## Interactivity

Interactive plots via ggiraph

- [`ggPSE_interactive()`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE_interactive.md)
  : Interactive periodic table with hover tooltips

## Data

Built-in element datasets

- [`ggpse_elements`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggpse_elements.md)
  : Full element properties table
- [`ggpse_grid`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggpse_grid.md)
  : Minimal element grid for plotting

## Package

- [`ggPSE-package`](https://vjgeiger.github.io/ggPSE/reference/ggPSE-package.md)
  : ggPSE: Periodic Table Visualization Using ggplot2
